claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"The single total family defined in proof.md Section 1: f_0=0; for n>=1 let k be the least prime with k^5>32n^3; if n<=k then f_n=0; else the first k bits give the monic polynomial Q=Z^k+sum b_j Z^j, and f_n=0 unless Z^(2^k)=Z mod Q and gcd(Q,Z^2+Z)=1; if so, with K=F_2[Z]/(Q), m=n-k, r=ceil(m/k), t=ceil(sqrt(r)), pad the remaining m bits with zeros to r blocks of k bits read as y_i in K via the polynomial basis, and output Tr(Sym_r^t(y_1^(2^(r+1)-1), y_2^(2^r-1), ..., y_r^(2^2-1))) with Tr the absolute trace K->F_2.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"2","numerator":"7"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"2","numerator":"7"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one total uniform polynomial-time family, hence in NP with empty witnesses, every circuit in the full Li-Yang B2 model computing f_n has at least (7/2)n - 56 n^(4/5) - (35/2) n^(3/5) - 7 gates for every integer n >= 10^7, all k prefix bits being counted in n; hence C_B2(f_n) >= (7/2)n - o(n) at every sufficiently large integer length n = |x|.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}
